title: SoccerNet Game State Reconstruction: End-to-End Athlete Tracking and Identification on a Minimap
summary: Formalises game-state reconstruction: track and identify players from one broadcast camera onto a 2D minimap. Introduces SoccerNet-GSR, GS-HOTA metric and a TrackLab-based baseline.

title: Scaling up SoccerNet with multi-view spatial localization and re-identification
summary: SoccerNet-v3: 1.3M annotations on 33,986 broadcast/replay images (lines, players, jersey numbers, cross-view links) for calibration, localisation and multi-view re-identification.

title: No Bells, Just Whistles: Sports Field Registration by Leveraging Geometric Properties (extended as PnLCalib)
venue: CVPR Workshops 2024; extension in Computer Vision and Image Understanding 2026
summary: Camera calibration from broadcast frames via detected pitch keypoints and lines; the PnLCalib extension refines parameters by minimising line reprojection error.

title: A General Framework for Jersey Number Recognition in Sports Video
summary: Adapts scene-text recognition to jersey numbers, aggregates per-frame predictions over tracklets; reports 87.4% tracklet accuracy on SoccerNet, plus a public hockey dataset.

title: WorldPose: A World Cup Dataset for Global 3D Human Pose Estimation
who: Jiang, Billingham, Müksch et al. (ETH Zürich, FIFA)
summary: 88 sequences, 2.5M+ SMPL 3D player poses from 2022 World Cup multi-camera capture, with moving broadcast-camera calibration; released for academic research.

title: roboflow/sports: open-source computer vision tools for sports
summary: Open repo and datasets for soccer player, ball and pitch-keypoint detection; demo combines tracking, SigLIP-based team clustering and a homography 'radar' minimap.

title: SoccerNet 2025 Challenges Results
summary: Fifth annual open SoccerNet benchmark: team ball-action spotting, monocular depth, multi-view foul recognition and game-state reconstruction; summarises leading methods.

title: SoccerMaster: A Vision Foundation Model for Soccer Understanding
summary: One multi-task pretrained visual model covering soccer tasks from athlete detection and identification to event classification, using an automated annotation pipeline (SoccerFactory).

title: TacticAI: an AI assistant for football tactics
who: Wang, Veličković, Hennes et al. (Google DeepMind, Liverpool FC)
summary: Geometric deep learning on corner kicks predicts receivers and shots and proposes repositionings; Liverpool FC experts preferred its suggestions 90% of the time.

title: Game Plan: What AI can do for Football, and What Football can do for AI
who: Tuyls, Omidshafiei, Muller et al. (DeepMind, Liverpool FC)
summary: Agenda-setting paper arguing football analytics needs combined statistical learning, game theory and computer vision; sketches an automated video assistant coach.

title: A Graph Neural Network deep-dive into successful counterattacks
summary: GNNs on tracking-data graphs from 632 MLS, NWSL and international women's games predict counterattack success; gender-specific models beat pooled ones.

title: un-xPass: Measuring Soccer Player's Creativity
summary: Rates passing creativity as passes that are both unlikely and valuable, combining pass-selection, success and value models on StatsBomb 360 freeze-frames.

title: Evaluating passing decision-making in professional football: An enhanced MPNN approach to Receiver Selection
summary: Message-passing GNN over player graphs (edges: distance, angle, pressure) predicts the chosen pass receiver; tracking and events synchronised with Needleman-Wunsch alignment.

title: Maximising the Set-Piece Return: Optimising Football Corner Tactics with Graph Reinforcement Learning
summary: Graph-based RL policy adjusts attackers' positions and velocities at corners to maximise first-contact shot probability; evaluated on 3,000+ Premier League corners.

title: Towards a foundation large events model for soccer
summary: Large Events Model: tokenised next-event predictors that simulate matches from any game state; applied to xP+, a player's contribution to team points.

title: Seq2Event: Learning the Language of Soccer Using Transformer-based Match Event Prediction
summary: Transformer predicts the next event's type and location from preceding events; uses predictions to build poss-util, a possession utility metric.

title: A Foundation Model for Soccer
summary: Proof-of-concept transformer trained on three seasons of league event data to predict subsequent actions, compared against Markov and MLP baselines; code released.

title: EventGPT: Capturing Player Impact from Team Action Sequences Using GPT-Based Framework
summary: Player-conditioned GPT-style model predicts next action type, location, timing and value; swapping player tokens enables counterfactual transfer-fit simulations.

title: Ball Trajectory Inference from Multi-Agent Sports Contexts Using Set Transformer and Hierarchical Bi-LSTM
summary: Infers the ball's trajectory from player tracking alone using a Set Transformer and hierarchical Bi-LSTM, useful when ball data are missing or noisy.

title: Sports-Traj: A Unified Trajectory Generation Model for Multi-Agent Movement in Sports
summary: UniTraj treats prediction, imputation and recovery as one masked-trajectory task with a Mamba-based encoder; releases Basketball-U, Football-U and Soccer-U benchmarks.

title: Unified Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion for Multi-Agent Trajectory Modeling
summary: U2Diff: diffusion model for multi-agent trajectory completion (e.g. correcting tracking data) with per-state uncertainty estimates; evaluated on sports datasets including soccer.

title: GenTac: Generative Modeling and Forecasting of Soccer Tactics
summary: Diffusion framework sampling diverse long-horizon multi-player trajectories and events from tracking data, conditionable on opponent, team or league style and objectives.

title: Google Research Football: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Environment
who: Kurach, Raichuk, Stańczyk et al. (Google Research)
summary: Open 3D football simulator for RL with benchmark tasks and 'academy' scenarios; pre-2021, but the testbed for most later multi-agent football RL.

title: TiKick: Towards Playing Multi-agent Football Full Games from Single-agent Demonstrations
summary: Offline multi-agent RL learns full 11-vs-11 Google Research Football games from single-agent replay demonstrations.

title: TiZero: Mastering Multi-Agent Football with Curriculum Learning and Self-Play
summary: Trains a full multi-agent Google Research Football team from scratch with curriculum learning and self-play, outperforming earlier systems.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative, Multi-Agent Games
summary: MAPPO: standard PPO with centralised value functions is a strong multi-agent baseline, including on Google Research Football scenarios.

title: From motor control to team play in simulated humanoid football
summary: Simulated humanoids learn from motion-capture priors and multi-agent RL to dribble, pass and coordinate in 2v2 football.

title: Learning agile soccer skills for a bipedal robot with deep reinforcement learning
who: Haarnoja, Moran, Lever et al. (Google DeepMind)
summary: Deep RL trains a 20-joint miniature humanoid for 1v1 soccer in simulation and transfers zero-shot to real robots, outperforming scripted skills.

title: Learning Vision-Driven Reactive Soccer Skills for Humanoid Robots
summary: Single RL controller couples onboard vision with locomotion for ball search, chasing and kicking; tested in real RoboCup competitions.

title: Designing a skilled soccer team for RoboCup: exploring skill-set-primitives through reinforcement learning
summary: Open Python codebase and RL skill primitives behind FC Portugal's RoboCup 3D Simulation League titles in 2022 and 2023.

title: SoccerNet-Caption: Dense Video Captioning for Soccer Broadcasts Commentaries
summary: Introduces single-timestamp dense captioning of full broadcasts, with almost 37k timestamped commentaries as benchmark data.

title: MatchTime: Towards Automatic Soccer Game Commentary Generation
summary: Re-aligns noisy commentary timestamps to video at scale, adds a manually aligned 49-match test set, and trains a video-LLM commentary generator.

title: Towards Universal Soccer Video Understanding
summary: SoccerReplay-1988 dataset (1,988 full matches) and MatchVision encoder for event classification, commentary generation and multi-view foul recognition.

title: Multi-Agent System for Comprehensive Soccer Understanding
summary: SoccerWiki knowledge base, SoccerBench (~10K multimodal multiple-choice QA, 13 tasks) and SoccerAgent, a multi-agent LLM system for soccer questions.

title: SoccerRAG: Multimodal Soccer Information Retrieval via Natural Queries
summary: Retrieval-augmented LLM framework answering natural-language questions over a multimodal SoccerNet-based soccer database.

title: SPORTSQL: An Interactive System for Real-Time Sports Reasoning and Visualization
who: Martinez, Ahuja, Bardoliya et al. (Arizona State)
summary: LLM text-to-SQL over live Fantasy Premier League data with automatic charts; DSQABench provides 1,700+ annotated queries.

title: Automated Explanation of Machine Learning Models of Footballing Actions in Words
summary: 'Wordalisation': turns logistic-regression xG coefficients into sentences, then an LLM narrates each shot for coaches and commentators; open interactive app.

title: SPORTU: A Comprehensive Sports Understanding Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multi-sport benchmark, soccer included, testing LLMs and multimodal LLMs on rules, strategy and video-based scenario reasoning.

title: The training—injury prevention paradox: should athletes be training smarter and harder?
summary: Influential review arguing high chronic workloads protect against injury and popularising the acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR).

title: Mathematical coupling causes spurious correlation within the conventional acute-to-chronic workload ratio calculations
summary: Shows coupled ACWR (acute week included in chronic window) induces spurious correlation between acute and chronic load.

title: Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio: Conceptual Issues and Fundamental Pitfalls
venue: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance 15
summary: Argues ACWR's causal link to injury is unestablished and ratio artefacts make it inaccurate, so manipulating it to cut injuries is conjecture.

title: What Role Do Chronic Workloads Play in the Acute to Chronic Workload Ratio? Time to Dismiss ACWR and Its Underlying Theory
summary: Random chronic loads gave similar injury associations; ACWR barely beat an intercept-only model, so authors recommend dismissing it.

title: Effective injury forecasting in soccer with GPS training data and machine learning
summary: Interpretable ML injury forecaster built from one season of GPS training-workload data at a professional club.

title: Forecasting football injuries by combining screening, monitoring and machine learning
summary: Prospective study of 88 professional players: gradient boosting on screening plus monitoring data reached only ROC AUC ~0.61-0.62.

title: Just How Confident Can We Be in Predicting Sports Injuries? A Systematic Review of the Methodological Conduct and Performance of Existing Musculoskeletal Injury Prediction Models in Sport
summary: Review of 30 studies (204 models): none externally validated, 98% high or unclear risk of bias; no model recommended for practice.

title: A large-scale multivariate soccer athlete health, performance, and position monitoring dataset
summary: SoccerMon: two seasons from two elite Norwegian women's teams; 33,849 subjective wellness/load reports plus GPS data with 6+ billion position samples.

title: Semi-automated offside technology (FIFA World Cup 2022)
summary: 12 roof cameras track up to 29 body points per player at 50 Hz; connected-ball IMU reports at 500 Hz; AI alerts video officials.

title: Semi-automated offside technology to be introduced in Matchweek 32
summary: Premier League adopted optical-tracking SAOT from 12 April 2025; the VAR still confirms kick-point and body parts before decisions.

title: VARS: Video Assistant Referee System for Automated Soccer Decision Making from Multiple Views
summary: Introduces SoccerNet-MVFoul, a multi-view foul video dataset, and a model classifying foul type and severity from synchronised camera views.

title: X-VARS: Introducing Explainability in Football Refereeing with Multi-Modal Large Language Models
summary: Video-language model that classifies fouls and explains decisions per the Laws of the Game; SoccerNet-XFoul has 22k+ referee-annotated QA triplets.

title: Video assistant referees (VAR): The impact of technology on decision making in association football referees
summary: 2,195 matches in 13 countries: 9,732 VAR checks, 795 reviews; decision accuracy rose from 92.1% to 98.3% after intervention.

title: Monitoring experts: insights from the introduction of video assistant referee (VAR) in elite football
summary: Natural experiment in Bundesliga and Serie A: VAR changed referees' decision-making, but home-team favouritism declined only partly.

title: Causal effects of an absent crowd on performances and refereeing decisions during Covid-19
summary: Ghost games in 17 countries: without spectators, referees' yellow-card bias against away teams shrank significantly, evidence of crowd social pressure.

title: Social pressure in the stadiums: Do agents change behavior without crowd support?
summary: Five European leagues: home advantage roughly halved behind closed doors, and fouls, cards and penalties became more balanced.

title: Hudl Statsbomb free Women's Euro 2025 data
summary: Free event and 360 freeze-frame data for all 31 UEFA Women's Euro 2025 matches, via the open-data repo (competition 53, season 315).

title: Hudl Statsbomb free women's league data (WSL, Liga F, Frauen-Bundesliga, Serie A, NWSL)
summary: Free data for 771 matches: 2023 NWSL plus full 2023/24 WSL, Liga F, Frauen-Bundesliga and Serie A Women seasons.

title: Explaining the difference between men's and women's football
summary: Classifier on World Cup event data separates men's and women's matches; explanations point to play accuracy, ball-recovery time and performance quality.

title: Understanding gender differences in professional European football through machine learning interpretability and match actions data
summary: Interpretable classifiers on Euro 2016 (men) and Euro 2017 (women) event data identify which match actions differ by gender.

title: Women's football analyzed: interpretable expected goals models for women
venue: IJCAI 2021 Workshop on AI for Sports Analytics (AISA)
summary: GAM xG models on 9,076 league matches (2,100 women's): models largely transfer across genders, though some shot types are valued differently.

title: Research on women's football: a scoping review
who: Okholm Kryger, Wang, Mehta et al.
summary: Scoped 1,634 women's football studies (1939-2019): mostly sports medicine and elite senior players; output still not comparable to men's football.

title: “Invisible Sportswomen”: The Sex Data Gap in Sport and Exercise Science Research
venue: Women in Sport and Physical Activity Journal 29
summary: Audit of 5,261 sport-science papers (2014-2020): 6% female-only, 31% male-only; 34% of all participants were female.

title: Estimating transfer fees of professional footballers using advanced performance metrics and machine learning
summary: ML with advanced performance metrics beats linear regression for transfer-fee prediction; used to rank clubs on value-for-money signings.

title: The wisdom of crowds and transfer market values
summary: Tests Transfermarkt crowd-sourced values against actual fees: crowd values are biased predictors, notably understating fees for players from top leagues.

title: Are Sports Betting Markets Semi-Strong Efficient? Evidence From the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: Bookmakers and exchanges overestimated home-win probability early in ghost games, mainly in the Bundesliga: temporary semi-strong inefficiency.

title: Home advantage in professional soccer and betting market efficiency: The role of spectator crowds
summary: 6,120 German matches (2011-2021): odds missed the short-run ghost-game drop in home advantage but priced it correctly in the long run.

title: AI-Based Video Clipping of Soccer Events
who: Valand, Kadragic, Hicks et al. (SimulaMet, Forzasys)
summary: ML pipeline finding start and end points for event highlight clips in soccer broadcasts, aiming to replace manual clipping.

title: PLayerTV: Advanced Player Tracking and Identification for Automatic Soccer Highlight Clips
summary: Detection, tracking, jersey OCR and colour analysis generate player-specific highlight clips; tested on Norwegian Eliteserien footage.

title: Premier League announces partnership with Microsoft
summary: Five-year deal; Copilot-powered Premier League Companion answers fan questions using 30+ seasons of stats, 300,000 articles and 9,000 videos.

title: Weekend idea: broadcast clip to minimap
summary: IDEA: Run roboflow/sports or sn-gamestate on a SoccerNet-GSR clip, project players onto a minimap, then compute team compactness and distance covered.

title: Weekend idea: pass-receiver GNN on freeze-frames
summary: IDEA: Turn StatsBomb 360 freeze-frames into player graphs and train a small GNN to predict pass receivers versus a nearest-teammate baseline.

title: Weekend idea: mini large events model
summary: IDEA: Train a tiny next-event transformer on StatsBomb open events, simulate thousands of possessions, and compare with a Markov-chain baseline.

title: Weekend idea: ask-the-data SQL bot
summary: IDEA: Load StatsBomb open events into DuckDB, have an LLM write SQL for 30 hand-checked questions, and measure execution accuracy.

title: Weekend idea: replicate the ghost-game effect
summary: IDEA: With free football-data.co.uk results and card counts, compare home win rate and card gaps before, during and after 2020-21 ghost games.

title: Weekend idea: does a men's xG model transfer?
summary: IDEA: Train xG on StatsBomb men's open data, test on Women's Euro 2025 shots, and compare calibration against a women-only model.
